built Graphael— a static AI/ML supply-chain intelligence tool that goes beyond flat package lists to build a source-level dependency graph, enriched with CVE intelligence and actionable remediation paths.
Most existing SBOM and SCA tools answer one question: what packages are declared?
Graphael asks a harder one: what does this repository actually depend on, at the source level, and what does that exposure look like?

That distinction matters more in AI/ML codebases than anywhere else. A single repository can contain training scripts, notebooks, model loading code, optional dependency ranges, build dependencies, and runtime dependencies — often with no clean separation between them. Package-first scanners miss the full picture. Graphael is built around the source tree itself.
It runs a fully static pipeline — no installs, no code execution, no runtime side effects: Stage 1 · LLMBOM generation

Stage 2 · Dependency Graph Construction Stage 3 · Threat Intelligence Augmentation Stage 4 · Adaptive Vulnerability Resolver Stage 5 · Iterative Patch Convergence Engine Stage 6 · Final output and audit reports

Our project, "Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts", addressed a key challenge in robotics: versatility in interacting with diverse input modalities and adaptability to specific use cases.

Video Gesture Recognition: Leveraging MediaPipe for real-time hand tracking, using the Computer Vision techniques.
Speech Recognition: Utilizing Speech Recognition library, we provided high-accuracy real-time transcription.
Text Processing: Through a fine-tuned BERT model, we perform command classification.

I'm excited to share my incredible journey during my internship at CAVE LABS-PESU, where my teammate Kiran Choudari and I collaborated on building an interactive ECG-based heart simulation using Unity and Three.js.
As someone passionate about bridging tech and healthcare, this project was especially meaningful to me. We integrated real ECG data (from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database) and processed it in Python to generate:
● A JSON file with ECG phase timings (P-wave, QRS complex, T-wave)
● Another file with waveform values for real-time plotting
These powered synchronized animations in Unity and Three.js, where the heart beats in sync with actual cardiac signals. I was particularly involved in tuning the speed control system — which allows users to slow down or speed up the simulation and observe cardiac phases in detail.
We also implemented a reverse ECG waveform generator from the animation, helping validate the model's accuracy — a challenging but rewarding part of the project.
I'm incredibly grateful for the mentorship of Prof.from the Center for Augmented and Virtual Environments (CAVE), and the continuous support from our mentor. A special thanks to our seniorsandfor their guidance throughout.
